facts: AstroMLab 5 aims to create structured summaries from 400,000 astrophysics papers.
Yuan-Sen Ting is affiliated with The Ohio State University.
Alberto Accomazzi is associated with the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics.
Tirthankar Ghosal works at Oak Ridge National Laboratory.
The dataset comprises 408,590 astrophysics papers from arXiv covering the period from 1992 to July 2025.
It includes the extraction of 9,999 unique concepts with detailed descriptions.
The dataset contains 3.8 million paper-concept associations.
The concept vocabulary and embeddings are publicly available at https://github.com/tingyuansen/astro-ph_knowledge_graph.

The deployment of large language models (LLMs) is advancing in materials science and chemistry. The astronomy literature lacks well-curated text resources. A centralized effort is proposed to create structured summaries and concepts from all astro-ph papers. The initiative aims to provide a dataset of 408,590 papers and 9,999 unique concepts.
The chosen method for converting astrophysics PDFs to machine-readable text is OCR.
Nougat (Blecher et al., 2023) was initially used to convert PDFs to markdown format.
The transition to Mathpix OCR API occurred in November 2024.
Inspections of Mathpix's output for approximately 50,000 papers showed no systematic errors.

The summarization approach divides academic papers into approximately 10,000-character segments at section boundaries. The compression system prioritizes retaining LaTeX formulas and key technical jargon. Over $50,000 in API costs were incurred for summarizing 408,590 papers. Raw summaries are reorganized into seven structured sections for enhanced analysis.
The methodology aims to identify approximately 10 novel concepts per paper.
Each concept includes a concise name, a classification, and a detailed description.
The final vocabulary consists of 9,999 concepts after manual review.
The methodology emphasizes the importance of scrutiny when utilizing the dataset.
The new vocabulary achieves complete coverage of all 408,590 papers.
The average number of concepts per paper in the new vocabulary is 9.4.
Traditional ADS keywords are author-supplied and lack systematic curation.
The new vocabulary is superior to abstracts for discovery tasks in academic research.
The concept vocabulary allows for precise tracking of idea emergence in astrophysics.
A notable peak in new concept emergence occurred in 2007 due to changes in arXiv's cross-listing policies.
Deep learning has dominated recent concept emergence in astrophysics.
Co-occurrence analysis shows increased integration of computational methods with traditional astrophysical domains over time.
The dataset includes all astro-ph papers from 1992 to July 2025.
The public release includes a CSV of concept vocabulary with labels, names, classes, and descriptions.
The dataset features 1.67 million unique identifiers for both internal and external citations.
Concept embeddings in the dataset use text-embedding-3-large.
The dataset contains 408,590 astrophysics papers from arXiv spanning the years 1992 to 2025.
It includes 9,999 AI-generated concepts with detailed descriptions.
Temporal analysis indicates a rise in machine learning in astrophysics from 2015 to 2025.
All code and data processing pipelines related to the dataset are publicly available.
The structured summary format for academic papers includes six semantic sections: Background, Motivation, Methodology, Results, Interpretation, and Implication.
USco1606-1935 is a candidate low-mass binary system identified using 2MASS data.
The methodology confirmed the binary nature of USco1606-1935 A and its potential association with B.
If confirmed as gravitationally bound, USco1606-1935 would be a rare example of a young multiple system.
